newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Wednesday mainly due to falls on the domestic A share markets, which led to decreased fund demand on the repo market, traders said.

The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract inched down at 7.48 percent from 7.50 percent on Tuesday. Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 1.8 million lots from 1.2 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the A market falls dampened sentiment on the repo market.
The absence of new A share issues also kept fund demand weak, traders said.
"Institutions, including securities houses, stayed on the sidelines today with fund demand falling, and this pushed down most of the repo rates," said one trader.

Traders said they believed the rates would move around the current level in the near-term but one new A share on the Shenzhen stock exchange on Friday would support the seven-day contract on Thursday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Wednesday led by a strong performance by the market leader, the 10-year bond maturing in 2006, traders said.
The bond was the most actively traded contract on Wednesday, rising sharply to 112.12 yuan from 111.35 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose sharply to 1.4 million lots from 511,984 lots.
"The sharp rise of the 10-year bond boosted market sentiment and led all the contract up," said one trader.
Spot contracts were expected to rise further on Thursday on improved sentiment, trader said.
